title: Help needed in my AI journey - Character Consistency
author: evening_child
selftext:
Hi everyone, I'm starting a new project in wanting to create an adult visual novel. I have experience in coding and game design, but I really can't draw well enough to suffice in the art department. For this reason I wanted to experiment with ai to try and come up with assets that are good enough to make the cut for my vn.   
The issue I've ran across is that I can't generate consistent enough pieces for them to feel like they belong to the same game. I know this is a common issue, but even after searching for resources online I haven't found a clear solution. I even read here and there that true asset consistency is currently not achievable, which tbh would be really discouraging since I don't see any other way to go about doing this other than using ai.    
Does anybody have any suggestions? Or maybe resources that I should check out in order to learn more about the topic?  
I've played a couple of vns that where based on ai generated images and seem to be really well executed on that front so I'm assuming there's a way around this issue somehow (?)  
One of the examples that I'm basing this assumption on is the adult vn "My Femboy Roommate" (nsfw obviously): it seems that basically every asset in that game has been ai generated but at the same tiem every piece appears to be coherent enough with the rest of the game. So I'm hopeful I can learn how to replicate what the author did to achieve such result.  
  
Thanks in advance, all advice is welcome!

comments.author: Tbhmaximillian
comments.body: Hey there, you can train LORAs with your character and then get a good result with image generation. to make it better afterwards or while creating your image you can use face swapping with a picture of your character. This is a quite simple solution to keep consistency. If you need better quality you need to google and get complexer workflows than what I told you. also feel free to drop a dm.

replies.author: evening_child
replies.body: Hey thanks a lot for the quick reply. I'll try that! Actually I'm already started on trying to train LORAs, though obviously I'm not sure whether I'm doing things right or not. Also thanks for the suggestion about face swapping, I hadn't thought of that

replies.author: Tbhmaximillian
replies.body: Youre welcome, always look for comfy workflows with the problem you have in mind. There are a lot of people that may have had the same problem and shared it with the world.

comments.author: goldenstormfish
comments.body: Have you tried Gemini? They recently launched Nano Banana (their image generator) which has amazing consistency

replies.author: positive_dialogue
replies.body: Yeah, I've had great experiences with Nano Banana compared to ChatGPT. I used it to generate an entire barn scene with animals in different poses for my game. I've never tried to generate adult content so I can't speak to the guardrails specifically.

comments.author: lordpoee
comments.body: A quick cheat is to use a PONY model with non-face altering LORA's. The have them wear what you want (or don't), grab the seed and generate using the seed. I have literally made hundreds of unique characters.

comments.author: Ashamed_Yam_5385
comments.body: I second on using LoRAs and personally, I edit every pic manually for my VN.

comments.author: KitsuMateAi
comments.body:
You need to keep the different types of consistency. 
Style consistency, character consistency, and overall consistency for good ai artworks. 

For style consistency, I suggest starting with using lora dedicated for specific style and consistent list of initial tags.

For character consistency, you have two options. 
Using character lora. Which is bothersome when you have to retrain lora every time you include new character. 

My second and preferable solution is to use 3d character as a reference. You can create it in a dedicated and somewhat easy to use program like vroid studio. Or, instead of creating one from scratch, use one from thousands available models as a base.

Then you can use vroid studio itself for posing or use other program. 

It ensures maximum control, allowing to generate poses or camera angles hardly achievable in image generators.

You can image created from such pose as an input for image generation for style transfer.

Last one, you have overall consistency (joined hair strands, malformed eyes or fingers).

For this one, either spam inpainting until desired results or just repaint it in paint to somewhat fixing it manually and use result again in inpainting. 

I don't know any effortless solution that would allow you to generate consistent images.
